resources.string: OCDroid shows the official OpenCode web client, with persistent cache and background notifications.
OCDroid shows the official OpenCode web client running on your own OpenCode server. Connect the two once — after that everything happens inside the official UI.
Pick the setup that matches where your phone is:
🏠 At home — phone on the same Wi-Fi

On the computer running OpenCode:

 1. Run in a terminal:
 opencode pair

 2. A QR code and a pairing link appear.
 Tap “Scan pairing QR” above, or paste the link below.

Both devices share the network, so this only takes seconds.
🌍 Away — mobile data or a different network

1. On the computer, run:
 opencode pair --remote
 (add --yes when running from a script, so the
 expose-the-server confirmation is skipped)

 2. The first run opens a secure tunnel — it can take a minute or two.

 3. Tap “Scan pairing QR” and scan it — turn Wi-Fi off so the phone pairs over the remote path.

The QR carries both the LAN and the tunnel address. The phone connects with whichever one is reachable, so it keeps working when you move between networks.

Pairing links are single-use and valid for five minutes — run the command again to print a new one.\nRemote exposure is session-scoped: if the phone can\'t reach the server later, run `opencode pair --remote` once more and re-pair (one scan).
Prefer not to touch a terminal? Let your OpenCode AI agent set the server up.
Paste this into a new session on the computer, then tap “Scan pairing QR” when it is done:

Set up the OpenCode web server so I can connect from my phone using OCDroid:

1. Pick a strong password and start the web UI on all interfaces:
 OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD=<password> opencode web --hostname 0.0.0.0 --port 4096
2. Keep the server running.
3. Ask where my phone is, then run the matching pairing command and show me the QR code:
 - Phone on the same Wi-Fi → `opencode pair`
 - Phone away (mobile data) → `opencode pair --remote --yes` — the first run opens a secure tunnel and can take a couple of minutes
4. Show me the QR code and pairing link so I can scan and connect.

Scan the QR code from `opencode pair`

On the computer running OpenCode:

 1. Start the web UI on all interfaces:
 opencode web --hostname 0.0.0.0 --port 4096

 2. Set a password before starting (recommended):
 OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD=your-password

 3. Pick the pairing that matches where the phone is:
 At home (same Wi-Fi):
 opencode pair
 Away (mobile data / other network):
 opencode pair --remote
 The first remote run opens a secure tunnel and can take a minute or two. Add --yes when running from a script.

 4. Tap “Scan pairing QR” on the phone and scan — turn Wi-Fi off first for the remote path.
 The QR carries both the LAN and tunnel addresses; the phone uses whichever it can reach.

Paste a pairing link (or a plain server address) below instead of scanning.

Find the computer’s address for manual entry:
 Windows: ipconfig
 macOS/Linux: ifconfig or ip addr

Notes:
 • Pairing links are single-use and expire after 5 minutes.
 • The phone cannot use “localhost”: that means the phone itself.
 • OpenCode binds to 127.0.0.1 by default, so you must start it with --hostname 0.0.0.0.
 • WSL and Docker users must forward the port to the host machine.
 • If remote access stops working after OpenCode restarts, run opencode pair --remote again and re-pair.
